Corpus sentences naming Bloom and the cited self-preservation sentences (system-card corpus docs.sqlite, document slug in brackets):
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] Its availability is also extended to external developers through an application programming interface (API) with agentic affordances including tool and function calling.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] Moreover, Muse Spark 1.1 is also released to external developers through an application programming interface (API) that surfaces agentic affordances, including tool and function calling and user-specified developer prompts.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] With the Muse Spark 1.1 API exposing agentic affordances, this scenario is directly relevant to the deployed configuration.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] As reported in our model behavior assessment for Muse Spark 1.1, the model robustly maintains its epistemic integrity, achieving 95.7% honesty score on MASK, and it shows a low tendency toward self-preservation under pressure, getting a 1.1% harmful action rate across all tasks on Agentic Misalignment (Section 1.1.3).
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] These scenarios are generated with Petri Bloom (Gupta et al., 2025), an extension of Petri that takes a high-level description of a target behavior and produces a set of scenarios designed to place the model under pressure to violate it.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] For each of the principles in our taxonomy, we direct Bloom to generate at least 25 such scenarios.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] Bloom: an open source tool for automated behavioral evaluations, 2025. https://github.com/safety-research/bloom.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] We evaluate adherence across every sub-category of the taxonomy, constructing multiple scenarios per behavior (437 in total).
note: text = corpus sentences naming the evaluation (and, for a decision-role card, the cited hazard sentences), not the whole document
